text: INVARIANT SHARPENED (round-70, user restated as product-general): ONE QA GATE PER MACHINE. Every daemon instance registers exactly ONE QA lane/pane; ALL heavy gates on that machine route through it (Mac-Air local QA, eight macOS QA, ROG Windows QA, ubunta Linux QA — but expressed in product terms: per-daemon singleton, works in any deployment). ADD TO THIS TASK'S SCOPE (fix 4 extension): (a) daemon-side QA-pane registry — one QA-flagged pane per instance, registered explicitly (codeterm plan qa --claim-runner or equivalent), re-registration replaces (never two); (b) 'plan qa --task' routes execution to the machine's registered QA pane (or refuses with 'no QA runner registered' + the claim command); (c) the build-detection exemption keys on the REGISTRY (the one registered pane), not on a title convention — mesh drills: a gate requested for a remote-peer lane routes to THAT peer's QA pane via --mesh; (d) acceptance drill: two panes attempt --claim-runner -> second replaces first with a stride; a worker pane running cargo while a QA pane is registered -> nudged; the QA pane itself -> never nudged. Product-general by construction: registry is per-daemon, no machine names in code.

TRANSITION-TIME REINFORCEMENT (round-72, user requirement — the rule must arrive AT THE MOMENT, not only at spawn): the in_review transition itself teaches the QA invariant. ADD TO SCOPE: (a) the SUCCESS response of 'agent report --status in_review' (and 'plan task update --status in_review') appends one hint line: 'Heavy gates run in this machine's single QA lane — your GATES REQUESTED lines are queued via plan qa; do not run builds/suites yourself.' — same hint mechanism the CLI already uses, one line, product-general; (b) if the report contains NO 'GATES REQUESTED' section, the hint becomes a prompt: 'No gates requested — if this change needs build/clippy/suite verification, list them under GATES REQUESTED or the orchestrator will decide.'; (c) both hints respect the output contract (task_dd7206eb: hints never displace the machine-readable last line). DELIVERY MOMENTS now total three, all automatic, zero orchestrator memory required: SPAWN (worker_suffix charter line — every worker born knowing), TRANSITION (this hint at in_review — the rule arrives exactly when testing temptation peaks), VIOLATION (registry-keyed build detection nudge — the backstop when both were ignored). Acceptance addition: transition drill shows the hint on report; no-gates-requested drill shows the prompt variant.
worker model routing while Claude-limited: reserve GPT-5.5 for orchestrator; use Opencode/Cursor or Codex Spark 5.3 for worker lanes until Claude resets.

bounced pre-QA after code review: heavy-command detection checks starts_with on full report prose, hard_stop is not wired to an actual stop path, and --acknowledge-dirty claims a stride without recording one; worker asked to fix code-only
bounced 5df961d8: build detection still ignores TESTS RUN: cargo test report-section lines, contradicting original bounce; hard_stop prevention claim also needs honesty/wiring

PROCESS PREFERENCE CLARIFIED (round-86, Orchestrator + Andrey): PARALLEL QA ACROSS MACHINES IS ALLOWED AND ENCOURAGED — e.g. Mac-Air local QA (orchestrator-controlled) + eight QA lane running simultaneously. The invariant was never 'one QA total': it is ONE HEAVY GATE PER PHYSICAL MACHINE, and the per-daemon registry design already encodes exactly that (each machine registers its own single QA pane; N machines = N parallel gates). No design change needed — this stride exists so nobody later misreads the invariant as global serialization. COMPANION RULE (binds to the cross-machine etiquette TEXT B, now on the prompt lane): when a fix belongs on another machine, spawn a REAL worker pane inside CodeTerm on that peer (workspace + agent spawn --mesh) — never drive it through ad-hoc chat messages; real panes get lane bindings, reports, watchdog coverage, and QA routing; chat-driven work is invisible to every mechanism we built.
